source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Norwalk campus, NYM5, publishes 4 MW of IT capacity and 168,000 square feet of technical space, and it is the largest data center by published capacity in Connecticut.

The published specification is the megawatt figure. The operator does not publish an address, a postal code, or a rack count, so the density of the hall is not stated. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 4 MW of IT load is roughly 100 racks. That figure is an assumption about rack power, not a number CyrusOne reports, and at a lower density such as 10 kW per rack the same 4 MW would support about 400 racks. Everything about how the capacity is deployed is inference.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which speaks to controls over financial reporting rather than to the power or cooling redundancy an AI tenant would care about. It does not qualify the campus for any particular workload, and it says nothing about whether accelerators are hosted there. No other certifications, no power redundancy topology, and no cooling design are published on the spec page this site read.

Connecticut has five mapped facilities, but only two publish a megawatt figure, and those two total 8 MW. This campus holds half of all the published data center capacity this site has found in the state. The other three mapped facilities publish nothing, so the state's real total is unknown and almost certainly larger than 8 MW. A 4 MW campus is small against the gigawatt-scale builds that dominate AI training, and its significance in Connecticut is a function of how little else in the state publishes a number at all.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
